audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Mentre i mercati tradizionali sono chiusi per il fine settimana, analizziamo gli ultimi sviluppi. Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dello 0.19%, Shanghai è rimasto stabile. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei se fossero aperti.

Sul fronte dei mercati occidentali, nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha registrato un aumento dello 0.84%, il VIX è salito dello 0.64%, segnale di una maggiore incertezza. Il Dollar Index è sceso del 0.42%, mentre l'oro ha guadagnato lo 0.44%, raggiungendo i 4720 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio Brent è salito dell'1.23%, toccando i 101.29 dollari.

Passando agli asset digitali, che operano 24 ore su 24, il Bitcoin ha registrato un aumento dello 0.06%, raggiungendo i 80,238 dollari. Gli afflussi netti giornalieri negli ETF Bitcoin sono stati di -268.5 milioni di dollari, mostrando un'inversione al ribasso.

Sul fronte macro, nessun dato rilevante è previsto per oggi.

Infine, in termini di geopolitica, la situazione rimane tesa, con le esportazioni cinesi che mostrano una crescita del 14% ad aprile, nonostante l'incertezza geopolitica. Questo potrebbe avere implicazioni per il futuro delle relazioni commerciali, specialmente in vista della riunione tra Xi e Trump.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 
  Bitcoin si mantiene sopra gli ottantamila dollari, con una variazione positiva dell'1,23%. 
  Tuttavia, i flussi ETF hanno registrato una significativa uscita netta di 268,5 milioni di dollari. 
  Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato da prese di profitto, dato che il prezzo di Bitcoin ha raggiunto un massimo di 3 mesi.

  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum guadagna il 2,15%, portandosi a 2.317 dollari. 
  Solana registra un aumento del 6,77%, arrivando a 93,73 dollari. 
  Anche BNB mostra un incremento del 2,56%, quotato a 651,45 dollari.

  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 38, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 

While traditional markets are closed for the weekend, let's analyze the latest developments. The Nikkei closed down 0.19%, Shanghai remained essentially flat. This suggests a weak opening for European markets if they were open.

On the Western market front, in the previous session, the S&P 500 rose by 0.84%, the VIX increased by 0.64%, a sign of greater uncertainty. The Dollar Index fell by 0.42%, while gold gained 0.44%, reaching $4,720 per ounce. Brent crude oil rose by 1.23%, touching $101.29

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... 
Bitcoin recorded a 0.06% increase, reaching $80,238 Daily net inflows into Bitcoin ETFs were -$268.5 million, showing a downward reversal.

On the macro front, no significant data is expected today.

Finally, in terms of geopolitics, the situation remains tense, with Chinese exports showing 14% growth in April, despite geopolitical uncertainty. This could have implications for the future of trade relations, especially ahead of the meeting between Xi and Trump.

 Bitcoin is holding above eighty thousand dollars, with a positive variation of 1.23%. 
However, ETF flows have seen a significant net outflow of $268.5 million. 
This movement could be influenced by profit-taking, given that the Bitcoin price has reached a 3-month high.

Among altcoins, Ethereum gains 2.15%, reaching $2,317 
Solana records a 6.77% increase, reaching $93.73 
BNB also shows a 2.56% increase, quoted at $651.45

The Fear & Greed Index is at 38, in the Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors.

We are awaiting economic data due out today. For a deeper dive into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thanks for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Do Trump’s ‘maximum pressure’ sanctions inevitably lead to military action?
articles.snippet: Do Trump’s ‘maximum pressure’ sanctions inevitably lead to military action? Expert comment jon.wallace 8 May 2026 When ‘maximum’ economic pressure fails to bring regime change, and rhetoric has made diplomacy politically impossible, momentum towards military solutions will grow. During the first administration of President Donald Trump, the US imposed so-called ‘maximum pressure’ sanctions on five countries: Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria and Venezuela. In three of those cases, ‘maximum pressure’ was exerted by either creating new sanctions (Venezuela), tightening existing ones (Cuba) or returning sanctions that had been lifted (Iran). So, they were returned to Tehran from Moscow. Confronted with a threat that Ukraine has spent four years learning to counter, the United States found itself in unfamiliar territory. articles.title: Europe Is Losing the Energy-Security Battle to China
articles.snippet: While tensions around the Strait of Hormuz are rattling global oil markets, energy security is no longer defined solely by access to fossil fuels. What China has understood, and Europe has not, is that security now depends on electricity systems that can deliver low-cost power at scale and support heavy industry.

articles.title: The Missing Linchpin of European Hard Power
articles.snippet: Spurred by the Ukraine war and deepening doubts about America’s commitment to its NATO allies, Europe has begun building the financial and industrial foundations of military power. Unless it also establishes a clear political authority capable of directing that power, however, Europe could end up more vulnerable than ever.

articles.title: Could Russia Follow the “Hormuz Playbook” in the Baltic and Black Seas?
articles.snippet: On the eve of the U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran, 56 tankers sailed through the Strait of Hormuz. Two days later, Lloyd’s List, the maritime industry’s journal of record, counted just seven tankers and a single gas carrier — all small and three of them shadow-fleet vessels — with hundreds more drifting in the Gulf of Oman. One of the world’s most important maritime chokepoints had not been mined, blockaded, or seized by a navy. articles.title: India's Inflation Accelerates as High Energy Prices Start to Bite
articles.snippet: Inflation in India, the world’s third-biggest crude oil importer, accelerated in April as the higher global oil and gas prices started to feed through consumer prices. The annual consumer price index (CPI) is expected to have jumped to 3.8% in April, up from 3.4% in March, a Reuters poll of 46 economists showed on Friday. Responses in the poll, carried out between May 4 and May 8, ranged from 2.8% to 4.2%. Official data is expected on May 12. All economists concur that the effects of the higher energy prices have begun to take their toll…
